rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance (source of income and other tenant-selection limits)
rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers and rental agents may not discriminate in renting housing based on protected categories, including source of income (Section 8 and public benefits). Any tenant-selection standard must be reasonable and applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.
rules.key_value: Source of income (incl. Section 8) protected; uniform, reasonable selection standards only
rules.quoted_span: Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants
rules.effective_date_note: Documents do not state an effective date.
rules.exemptions: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
rules.penalty: Civil fines of up to $300 per violation, plus injunctive relief, damages and other relief after a hearing.

rules.title: Cambridge Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords must give tenants the city's Tenants Rights and Resources Guide when a tenancy starts and again when legal steps to end the tenancy are taken, such as a Notice to Quit or Summary Process. It does not bar evictions otherwise allowed by law.
rules.key_value: Guide required at start of tenancy and with any notice to quit or summary process
rules.quoted_span: It is required to provide this Guide at the inception and termination of tenancies
rules.effective_date_note: Documents do not state an effective date (page posted 2020-10-14).
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental agreements, including tenants at will and single-unit owner-occupied rentals.
rules.exemptions: Units in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities; short term rental units.
rules.penalty: Fine of $300 for each day's violation (Sec. 8.71.070).

non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facility units

no_rule_findings.finding: State law bars municipalities from enacting or enforcing rent control, so Cambridge has no local rent cap.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind

no_rule_findings.finding: Cambridge has only adopted a policy order directing the city manager to draft policy options or ordinance language on algorithmic rent pricing; no ordinance exists.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The policy order directs the city manager work with relevant city departments to draft policy options or ordinance language that will be presented back to council later this term
no_rule_findings.basis_citation: Cambridge City Council policy order (algorithmic rent pricing)
